meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm Meredith Kalinowski, Owen's mother, and I have a call at 4:40. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of class, and nobody called me. Who decided on that zero, Hale?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me what you based it on.

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Procedure 4.1 says you speak to the student first, Hale, so did anyone ask Owen about this before that zero went in?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2. Seventeen-year-olds misquote and paraphrase all the time, Hale, and editions differ, so how is a wrong line anything more than a bad citation?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing, nothing on his record, before I agree to anything. You still haven't answered me on that quotation, Hale.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You acknowledged in our meeting that the zero was entered before anyone contacted me, and you offered a supervised reassessment under procedure 4.4, on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that offer in writing, including the guarantee that nothing goes on his record, along with your answer on whether Owen was spoken to before the zero was entered and on the quotation you raised. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, with her demand that nothing go on his record met by your 4.4 offer, but she still wants that offer in writing and an answer on the quotation before she agrees to the rewrite; the private supervised rewrite you offered is the fair outcome, and she was one step from taking it, with time still left on her clock.
What moved her: you cited procedure 4.4 accurately and committed to it with a time, a supervisor and a clean record, because that met her one non-negotiable exactly.
What cost ground: you offered the rewrite before answering her challenge that a wrong quotation might just be a bad citation, and you never answered her question about speaking to Owen first, so your evidence was left half-tested and she had no reason to concede.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the document created after 11:30 the night before it was due and two large pastes minutes later, landed very close to that kind of night, which is why she went straight to procedure instead of asking about the times; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she argued that students misquote and editions differ, answer that before offering the rewrite, by letting her confirm the line appears in no edition and comparing it with Owen's other written work, then tell her plainly whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero.
